This page sets the editing standards for everyone who writes on the SWCCG Wiki, human or AI. The same rules apply to all editors. The wiki is an encyclopedia: a compendium of existing knowledge that is honest about where the knowledge comes from. Editors do not invent knowledge. == Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching) == '''Bill (2026-10-12; repeated many times):''' SWCCG is a small world. If a match is about '''99.8%''' likely to be the same person, treat them as one person and go with it. '''Never ask Bill to confirm near-certain matches.''' Skip only genuinely ambiguous cases. '''State near-certain matches plainly (Bill, 2026-10-13):''' once a match passes this rule, write it as fact. Do not add "(inferred)", "matched by name" or conflict/hedging notes on pages, tables or Talk pages. Keep factual spelling-variant notes (e.g. listed as "Clint Hayes"). This covers '''all''' identity matching: * '''Name variants:''' nickname or short form, middle initial, obvious typo, same events (Charlie/Charles, Matt/Matthew). * '''Nicknames and handles:''' forum shorthand (for example "BFred" for [[Brian Fred]]), and GEMP, Holotable, DeckTech, or Slack handles when context makes the match near-certain. * '''Photo identification:''' a tag or caption, the person's own comment, elimination within a tagged group, a nickname or handle plus thread or event context that makes the person near-certain, '''or''' a distinctive name plus a Decipher or SWCCG link (for example, a Decipher staffer of that name), with the reasoning on the page's Talk page (Bill, 2026-10-27). A photo may come from any source. Uncertain faces stay unidentified. * '''Exact name + Star Wars CCG Facebook group (Bill, 2026-10-30):''' an exact legal-name match already on the wiki who is a member of facebook.com/groups/starwarsccg is the same person; dest. Group membership is a Decipher/SWCCG link. Hometown match is extra color, not a gate. A public Intro with no SWCCG text does not block. Worked: [[John Petelle]]. Still skip locked identity traps and inexact names (Caputo ≠ Caputa). * '''Decklist and results attribution:''' last-name-only sheets, first name plus initial, Username boxes, and published nicknames — merge onto the identified player page when context makes the match about 99.8%. One canonical page per person; other names redirect. Link as [[Canonical|Name as in source]]. Add an "also known as" or handle note on the person page. '''Conflicting spellings.''' When name variants conflict, compare the sources (results, forums, decklists, videos) and use the best-supported name for the page; the other spellings are redirects, with a "sometimes spelled" note on the page. Example: [[JW Millet]] (also published as J.W. Miller and JD Millet). == Write for the reader == * '''Reader value decides what stays.''' Include a fact if it changes what a player understands or what a collector does. Cut it if it does not, even when it is true and sourced. Catalog bookkeeping, such as a rarity code or how an encyclopedia labels a pack slot, is not reader value. * '''Be concise.''' Use short, neutral sentences. Cut repetition and unnecessary detail. Cut words before facts. When a source has a long list, put it in one sentence and move on. Clarity and full understanding come first: a sentence or quote may be as long as clarity needs (Bill, 2026-10-26). * '''Describe the subject, not the sources.''' Write "X is Y", not "The Encyclopedia lists X as Y". Where the information came from belongs in the citation. * '''Minor facts are welcome.''' Many readers collect and never played, so short, sourced collector and pack facts, such as the original price of a pack, add to the article. * '''Give an example for an unusual rule.''' A concrete example makes a strange concept clear, for example "if both cards were in hand, they would be lost to [[Monnok]]". Not every rule needs one. * '''Lead with the fact (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' The first sentence says what the subject is and the most important thing about it. Context and background come after the facts, never before. * '''State facts plainly.''' When a reliable source, or Bill's own knowledge, supports a fact, state it directly ("Decipher showed Lucasfilm the card"). Do not soften it with "reportedly", "is said to", "appears to", or labels such as "soft" or "secondary". If a claim is genuinely disputed, name who says it ("According to Holland, ...") once, then move on. * '''No research notes in articles.''' The article body never contains process or meta text: no "research note", "this pass", "this page does not invent", "not found", "no source says", "unverified", and no Gaps, Open questions, Research, or Sources-checked sections. Open questions and empty searches go on the Talk page under Missing data. * '''Do not describe what an image shows.''' Captions identify the subject and credit the photographer ("Sealed first-series box. Photo: KaosBound."). Do not narrate visible content (art, colours, frames, which box is on the left). Quote printed text only when the text itself is the fact. * '''Captions don't say where a picture came from (Bill, 2026-11-04).''' Don't write "from LinkedIn", "his Facebook photo", "Photo: Reddit" or "Fair-use screenshot" in a caption, and don't put the source ref there. Just post the picture with its caption. The source, the Preserved copy and any fair-use note go on the File page. A photographer credit stays ("Photo: Decipher.", "Photo: teabo."). * '''Length discipline.''' Give readers enough sourced detail to understand the subject. Cover the people, chronology, relationships, features and concrete work that explain its significance. Add relevant detail when an article is too thin. Use prose for context and tables for catalogs or comparisons. Give each fact one clear home. * '''End directly.''' The last section ends on a fact, usually the outcome or the current state. No summary paragraph, no caveats, no "more research is needed". * '''One reference list.''' Use the References section only; do not add a separate Sources list that repeats it. * '''Filler check before saving.''' Search the body for "note", "research", "pass", "not found", "no source", "unverified", "soft", "reportedly", "appears", "Gaps", "Inferred". Rewrite each match as a plain fact or move it to the Talk page. "Inferred" is still allowed as a Talk-page or reference note (likely facts may be published marked inferred there); just do not put an "Inferred:" label in body prose. * '''Run the style lint (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' AI agents must run python3 authoring/style_lint.py draft.wiki --title "Page" (in the billbisco/swccg-wiki repo) and fix every flag before saving any article, then run style_lint.py "Page" on the live page after saving; never save with open flags. Human editors may run it too (optional). It flags hedge and meta words, Gaps/Notes/Research headings, a Sources heading outside deck and event pages, captions that describe the image, cited URLs without a Preserved copy, personal email addresses and empty refs, and reports the body word count against the previous revision. It has no sentence- or quote-length limit. == Cite your sources == * Important facts deserve a citation: numbers, dates, rules, and anything a reader might doubt. Not every sentence needs one. * When a fact is well established, add the reference and move on. * When a claim is disputed, doubtful, or an opinion, name the source in the sentence itself ("According to ..."). * '''Citation layout (Bill, 2026-10-20).''' Sources go in the References section as <ref> citations, each with its Wayback Machine Preserved copy inside the same ref: [https://example.com/page Title], site (date). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020000000/https://example.com/page Internet Archive]. An External links section is only for further reading, and its links are archived too. Only deck and event pages (decklists, tournaments, championships, Retro League events) keep a Sources section; every other page cites in References. * '''Every cited URL needs a checked Wayback copy (Bill, 2026-10-20).''' Every external URL on a page needs a Preserved copy, including links in lists, tables, body text and External links. The copy is a Wayback Machine capture (web.archive.org/web/ + 14-digit timestamp + the URL) or an Internet Archive item. Cite a copy only after it has been opened and checked, or verified against the source by the archive worker. Links to wiki.swccg.com and swccg.com/images need no copy. * '''Private source documents (Bill, 2026-10-12).''' When Bill provides private source documents (for example, an organizer's email), host them under swccg.com/snapshots/ (for example, snapshots/email/) and archive them like any other source, with a Preserved copy. * '''No personal email addresses on wiki pages (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Do not publish personal email addresses (player contacts, mailto strategy credits that only carry a private address, or emails embedded in Service rows). Keep callsigns, hometowns, dates, and citations. Drop an emptied email column. Exception: a clearly defunct, historically significant, non-personal address may stay (for example a Decipher corporate strategy credit such as joea@decipher.com). * '''Don't narrate source disagreements (Bill, 2026-10-13).''' When sources differ, state the best-supported fact and cite all the relevant sources on it. Explain the discrepancy on the Talk page, not in the article. Avoid sentences such as "Decipher announced 11 July; the Players Committee gives only Summer 2001." * '''Do not add inferences.''' If no source states it, it does not go in the article. Put the idea on the article's Talk page, labeled as an inference. == Accuracy == * Link card titles and use the exact card title, including the printing's own title (for example, the Alternate Image of [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo]] is [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo (AI)]]). * Give a price only where it shows something, such as an Alternate Image against the regular printing. A pack's original price is welcome. * Proofread and read the changes before saving. * '''Always give the deck's format (Bill, 2026-10-14).''' Every decklist page and table row names a format. If the source does not state it, use the smallest format that fits the newest set in the list and the date, and mark it "(from the card pool)". * '''Deck format comes from the tournament.''' A DeckTech post date does not determine a deck's format; use the tournament's format. For example, every FreedomCon 2001 deck is [[Premiere - Reflections III]]. == Holder and tenure tables == * '''No repeated person.''' Never repeat a person across rows when their tenure is continuous; show each name once on the row where they belong so one line shows their full tenure. * '''Merge identical adjacent rows.''' Merge adjacent rows with identical holders into one row with the combined date range. * '''Close gaps.''' Check for gaps between one holder's end and the next holder's start; research the true handoff date rather than leaving a gap. * '''One range, not capture dates.''' When nothing changed between documented dates, show one range from the start date to present (or to the last documented date if no longer current), not a list of capture dates. Never split a continuous tenure at a year or archive-snapshot boundary unless the role, team or title actually changed per a source. * '''Same role, one row.''' Abbreviations or wording variants of the same role (e.g. Dev = Developer) are one role: merge into one row with the full name. * '''Position first.''' In organization and roster lists, write every entry position first, then person (for example "Design Advocate: [[Chris Kelly]]"), including advocates, in the same format as team entries. Service roles inside teams (for example lead GEMP slicer) are positions too: write "Lead GEMP slicer: [[Jeremy DiPaolo]]", one sub-bullet per role, not "[[Jeremy DiPaolo]] (lead GEMP slicer)". == Photos of people == * '''Photo sources (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' A photograph of a person may come from any source. The only test is how certain it is that the photo shows the same person. * '''Small World Rule for photos (Bill, 2026-10-27).''' A distinctive name plus a Decipher or SWCCG link (for example, a Decipher staffer of that name) means the photo is taken as the same person. Record the reasoning on the page's Talk page. See [[#Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching)|Standing rule]]. * '''Facebook photographs (Bill, 2026-10-30; worked: [[Charles Lund]]).''' Dest the photograph as the wiki File (lead and Photographs; caption is the name, or the words printed in the frame). Preserve a screenshot of the Facebook surface as it appeared (photo viewer or group post) as the Route C snapshot: a short yellow banner with the date and live URL, then that screenshot. File page: who, Facebook, date, live URL, Preserved copy. Identification stays on Talk. The Facebook-chrome screenshot stays off Photographs. * '''Photo difficulty is not a skip (Bill, 2026-10-30).''' Dest the best available photograph of the person. Tiny circulars, AVIFs, and low-resolution faces dest as JPEG; the wiki scales them. Worked: [[Jindrich Nepevny|Jindřich Nepevný]] 88×88 circular. Do not HOLD for a failed circular click, AVIF, "need a larger JPEG", or a two-person frame when the subject is identifiable. * '''Repeating face in a group (Bill, 2026-10-30).''' When one face is present across several pictures, dest that person (crop of that subject + uncropped original in Photographs). Worked: [[Roberto Borias]] left-most face. * '''Memes and logos are not the lead.''' Skip a meme, logo, or product circular as the person lead; dest a real photograph of the person from the same profile. Worked: [[David Shettlesworth]] fish photograph instead of the meme circular. * '''Identify from evidence under the small-world rule.''' Name a person from a tag or caption on the source (or the person's own comment), by elimination within a tagged group, '''or''' from a nickname or handle plus thread or event context that makes the match about 99.8% certain (see [[#Standing rule: SWCCG is a small world (identity matching)|Standing rule]]). Mark anything truly uncertain as unidentified rather than guessing. * '''No obscene gestures on person pages (Bill, 2026-10-12).''' Do not put a photo that shows an obscene gesture (for example a middle finger) on a person page. Such a photo may be used only as an identification reference; do not upload it to the person page or display it there. * '''Cite the source and an archive copy.''' On the File page, link the source photo or post and add a preserved copy (Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/... Internet Archive]). If no archive can capture it, say so. * '''Credit the photographer only when known.''' Otherwise leave the photographer field blank. A still from a video is credited to the video's creator (the Players Committee YouTube channel is titled Star Wars CCG; credit those stills Players Committee). * '''New file names only.''' Never overwrite an existing file; check for duplicates on the wiki first. * '''Hunt a lead photograph (Bill, 2026-10-16).''' When creating or expanding a person page, hunt a sourced photograph and put it on the page. Video stills from SWCCG shows are allowed; crop StreamYard nameplates, host picture-in-picture, letterbox, and empty background out of stills so a single subject is centered. Do not leave a person page without a photograph when a sourced copy exists. * '''One lead photograph.''' If an objective is on the wrong side for the deck, it is a transcription error: leave the link and note it on the Talk page. == Tournament reports (Bill, 2026-10-24) == * '''One article per report.''' Decklists link the printing that was legal on the event date (see [[#Tournament and league pages|Tournament and league pages]]). == Card versions vs products (Bill, 2026-11-10) == A '''version''' is the printed object. Two copies are the same version when language, border, '''set icon''' (Premiere has none), foil, printed game text and stats, and copyright year all match. A '''product''' is the box or pack. Leftover or repacked copies of the same version (Enhanced Premiere Unlimited boosters, First Anthology starters, Reflections I–III bulk non-foils) are extra products on that article. They do not get a new article or another title parenthesis. '''Named editions''' of one version that were independently sold as constructed sets share one article. The title stacks those edition names in chronological order, first product first. English white Premiere with no expansion icon and ©1995 that shipped in both Premiere Two-Player (February 1996) and Premiere Unlimited (April 1996): [[Imperial Barrier (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)]]. The Players Committee lists revised wording on some of those reprints (Monnok, Grimtaash). They are not a third parenthesis on the 1995 white. Japanese black Premiere and Japanese white Two-Player are two versions because the border differs. Set hubs list every card the set contains and pipe the display name: [[Imperial Barrier (Premiere Two-Player) (Unlimited)|Imperial Barrier]]. Redirect the short names to the stacked title except where the short name is a different version (the Two-Player misprints). Infobox identity block, top to bottom: '''Set''' (primary product, first named edition). Then '''Set icon''' (printed expansion symbol, or none). Then '''Also in''' (other products of this version; omit when empty). Then Publisher, Era, and '''GEMP ID''' (first named edition first; two ids when two named editions). Gameplay '''Icons''' (Pilot, Warrior) stay with the face stats. GEMP: one wiki article and one uniqueness for one version. Two GEMP ids when that version is a named edition of two constructed sets (Premiere Two-Player first, then Unlimited). Leftover SKUs do not mint extra ids. A format can legalize Premiere Two-Player without Unlimited, and the reverse. swccg-guild/work#244. == Foreign-language card articles (Bill, 2026-11-05) == On English-language articles for a printing in another language, put a visible '''Title''' section near the top of the article body, before Card Text, showing the exact printed title in its original script. An infobox row is not enough. For Japanese printings, name the translation section '''Translation of Japanese Text'''. Place it below Lore and above Notes. Translate the title, lore and game text. Preserve separate edition articles such as [[Premiere Limited]], [[Premiere Unlimited]] and [[Premiere (Japanese)]]. For migrated families, edit the shared family template once and include it in each member article. Era and set headings are bold, underlined article links. Adding a publication requires its article and shared entry in the same batch, followed by checks of every member's membership and current selection. == Websites and sources == * '''Include the site's images (Bill, 2026-10-14; expanded 2026-10-16).''' An article about a website or source includes its relevant images (banners, deck or event graphics, home-page and section landing-page screenshots) from archived copies. Each File page gives the source and a preserved copy. * '''Creator and contributor credits (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Name the people or teams behind the project when the evidence identifies them. Distinguish a final expansion from a documented end of production, and distinguish later editions, reprints and fan continuations. * '''Playable versions (Bill, 2026-11-07).''' Describe the supported card pool and available modes, such as bot play and multiplayer, where documented. Credit the people who develop the online implementation separately from the original game's publisher and designers. == Cross-linking checklist (Bill, 2026-10-14) == When you create a page, add it to every index it belongs in, and create missing pages for what it mentions: * '''Fan site:''' the [[Fan sites]] table and [[:Category:Fan sites]]. * '''Facebook group:''' the [[Fan sites]] table, [[:Category:Fan sites]], the admin's Service row, and a screenshot of the group. * '''Decklist:''' a page for every list an article mentions. A link in See also or in a Tournament reports list does not count. A new player page always gets its results row, never an empty table. * '''People:''' named team members and organizers get player pages (stubs are fine), linked from the event and team. A personal opinion list (someone's Top 10) is not cross-referenced onto each named player's page. * '''Guests and features:''' guests on SWCCG video or audio shows, and subjects of written features, get a cited Appearances or In print row the same turn the host catalog records them. == Talk pages == Use an article's Talk page as the editors' notebook after any substantial edit. Useful sections are: * '''Missing data''': what you looked for and could not find or verify. * '''Possibly faulty data''': facts you doubt, with the conflicting sources. * '''Marginal cuts''': things you left out that another editor might want back, with their sources. * '''Build notes''': how a fact was traced, for the next editor. When tightening an article, move anything cut that may be useful (open questions, weak sources, cut text) to the Talk page under Missing data or Marginal cuts, so the article stays clean and nothing is lost. == Working together == * If you disagree with another editor's change, or think it is wrong or incomplete, say so and give your reason. * Once your concern has been heard and the decision stands, follow it. Speak up, then support the decision. * Check the current version of a page before editing, and apply your changes on top of other editors' wording rather than replacing it. * Use a short edit summary that says what changed. Those reprints are not listed. A foil of a title that is not on this list is not a Decipher Reflections III pack foil (it may be a [[Promotional Foils|promotional foil]] or a counterfeit).[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2].
